Week of 2026-07-20 to 07-27. The naval blockade nonetheless still held (ships redirected/disabled/boarded Saturday). Net: supply_chain_resilience 0.48->0.45 (second chokepoint disrupted), middle_east_stability 0.15->0.14 (Red Sea widening and peak-intensity bombing defined most of the week; the nascent, unconsummated pause keeps the slip small), global_gdp_growth_modifier 1.01->1.00 (sustained ~$100 oil bit harder - S&P -0.6%, Nasdaq -2% on the week, recession odds elevated), and nuclear_risk_level 0.35->0.34 (first mutual de-escalation in the conflict, though the blockade continues). Russia-Ukraine intensified on the deep-strike front: Ukraine flew one of its largest barrages (Russia claimed 571 drones downed in a night) and sparked a major fire at a Wildberries warehouse near St Petersburg, deepening fuel shortages and pressure on Putin, so russia_stability 0.28->0.27; two-front high-intensity combat (US-Iran bombing, Ukraine/Russia exchanges killing dozens, Lebanon) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,509,000->1,512,500. The naval blockade held and Houthi/Red Sea attacks continued. This drives middle_east_stability 0.14->0.13 (war widened with Saudi direct involvement and civilian-infrastructure targeting) and reverses last week's tentative de-escalation on nuclear_risk_level 0.34->0.35 (pause broke, Iran struck US bases, Trump threats resumed). Russia-Ukraine ground on with Ukraine's deep-strike campaign degrading Russian energy infrastructure further (drones hit ~13 more energy facilities Aug 2, causing local blackouts), sustaining fuel-shortage pressure on Moscow: russia_stability 0.27->0.26, and two-front high-intensity combat (US-Iran with Saudi involvement, daily Ukraine-Russia exchanges, Red Sea) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,512,500->1,516,000. Week of 2026-08-03 to 08-10. Markets priced the de-escalation in hard - Brent fell more than 7% on the week (~$83-86) and the S&P 500 hit a record close Friday in its strongest week since April. This drives middle_east_stability 0.13->0.15 (framework deal emerging, though still subject to unmet conditions - Iran demands US compensation, troop withdrawal, war-end, and 5-7% transit fees, and a Houthi tanker strike still hit a Saudi vessel Aug 5), nuclear_risk_level 0.35->0.33 (positive/constructive talks reverse the prior re-escalation), supply_chain_resilience 0.45->0.47 (partial reopening close, oil easing) and global_gdp_growth_modifier 1.01->1.02 (acute oil-shock drag unwinding further as equities rallied to records). Week of 2026-08-10 to 08-17. Russia-Ukraine produced a rare, publicized Ukrainian battlefield reversal: Kyiv completed its eight-month Oleksandrivka-axis counteroffensive (Jan 29-Aug 12), retaking ~745 sq km and 26 settlements and clearing Russia from nearly all of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast (~10,000 Russian troops killed per Zelenskyy), even as Russia intensified nightly combined strikes (12+ killed Aug 10-11, KN-23 North Korean missiles battle-tested) - this, plus the fresh 86-11 US Senate sanctions package and the Kremlin barring the anti-war Yabloko party from the September Duma elections, nudges russia_stability 0.25->0.24. Macro turned benign-to-positive: the S&P 500 hit records (clearing 7,800 for a third straight weekly gain) on softer-than-expected July CPI/PPI and an expected Fed hold, shrugging off Brent's climb to ~$87, so global_gdp_growth_modifier ticks 1.02->1.03. Week of 2026-08-17 to 08-24. Last week's Hormuz optimism collapsed: the 60-day US-Iran memorandum of understanding expired Aug 17 and Trump ruled out extending the ceasefire, declared no talks were underway (Aug 18), threatened to 'bomb the shit out of' Oman if it obstructed reopening the strait, and posted a 'New US Territory' image claiming 'total control' of Hormuz, while a senior Iranian official said Tehran would shift to a 'fully offensive' posture and mount a 'timely and precise' attack to break the US naval blockade (a carrier group was en route to replace USS Lincoln; the UAE detected a missile threat Aug 18). The Iran-Oman shipping framework announced last week did NOT translate into any reopening - Iran's preconditions (lift the blockade, withdraw US forces, permanently end the war) remain unmet and the blockade held all week. Markets re-priced the escalation: Brent surged ~6% to ~$94 (a second straight ~6% weekly gain, fully reversing the prior week's -7% relief rally), Houthis struck another Saudi vessel in the Red Sea, and Israel ramped up strikes on Lebanon and hit the Abu al-Duhur airbase in Syria. This reverses last week's tentative improvements: middle_east_stability 0.16->0.14 (deal collapsed, MOU expired, offensive threats, Lebanon/Syria widening - though Pezeshkian's Aug 21 signal that Tehran wants the war to end soon keeps the slip contained), nuclear_risk_level 0.32->0.34 (MOU lapse, 'fully offensive' threat, carrier surge and UAE missile scare), and supply_chain_resilience 0.47->0.45 (Brent back to ~$94, strait firmly not reopening, blockade entrenched). Macro turned mildly risk-off: the S&P 500 fell ~1.4% on the week to ~2% below its record as the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped ~5% on rising Treasury yields, Fed-independence worries ahead of Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address, and the renewed oil bid - so global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 1.03->1.02, partially unwinding last week's tick. Russia-Ukraine ground on at high tempo (mutual missile/drone barrages killing civilians; Russian strikes have damaged 300+ Ukrainian fuel stations over six months) with only limited diplomacy - Moscow said it is 'ready for new ideas' but only ones matching Putin's existing goals - so two-front combat lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,522,000->1,525,000 while russia_stability holds at 0.24 (the grind and the tentative Russian openness roughly offset, no decisive single-week mover). Excluded/watched: no new node - the Hormuz re-escalation is a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, not a discrete era-defining event; Trump's 'very positive' outreach to Kim Jong-un and the scaled-down US-South Korea exercises are a minor Korea de-escalation with no clean structural dimension and are offset by the Iran nuclear-risk move; frontier-AI activity stayed incremental (GPT-5.6 Sol/Luna updates, Claude Sonnet 5 pricing made permanent, Grok Imagine Image 2.0, Meta Muse Spark) after late-July flagships already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick; and the Indonesia M7.7 Flores earthquake (~70 dead) and record Japan/South Korea rainfall predate this window (Aug 13-14) and map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude.
